headline: Firmus, the Australian AI data-centre company that shelved its share sale on 9 Oct 2026, could be forced to buy back shares from Nvidia and Blackstone if it cannot revive its listing, the Australian Financial Review reports.
score_reason: Kept at 4: AFR's own reporting on confidential terms that follows the shelved IPO of 9 Oct 2026, but only its opening was readable and the terms are described as 'suggesting' rather than stated in full.
importance_line: Nvidia and Blackstone, two of Firmus's backers, and Firmus itself are affected first, as the clauses show how those investors protected themselves before the sale was shelved, but the agreements are confidential, AFR says only that they 'suggest' the free-securities terms, and whether any clause has been triggered is not stated.
summary: The Australian Financial Review reports that confidential agreements could force Firmus Technologies, the AI infrastructure company backed by chipmaker Nvidia and the asset manager Blackstone, to buy back shares from those two investors if it fails to revive its stock market listing, which it shelved on 9 Oct 2026 (our 9 Oct 2026 edition carried Reuters on this). The same agreements suggest that a select group of shareholders including Nvidia and Blackstone would receive free securities if the company does not manage a 25 percent return on investment guaranteed within three months of a failed listing, which the paper says puts Firmus on a collision course with the investors it relies on for financing.
notes: Only the two opening paragraphs of the AFR article were readable (subscription page, about 650 characters), so the summary stays inside them; full terms and any trigger are unknown. No other outlet carries it. New today versus our 9 Oct 2026 edition (Reuters, IPO shelved) and 10 Oct 2026 edition (Bloomberg, $30 billion valuation on $51 million revenue): the confidential buyback and free-securities terms.
